body.p: The Office Action dated May 28, 2024, and the references cited therein have been carefully studied and reviewed, and in view of the following representations, reconsideration is respectfully requested.

By this Amendment, claims 1, 3-5 and 11 have been revised, and new claims 15- 20 have been added. No new matter has been added. Support for the amendments and new claims can be found in the originally-filed application, including the specification, drawings and claims thereof.
Claims 1-20 are now pending in the application.

Claims 1-3, 6, 8-9, 11, 13 and 14 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Yamashita (US 2010275918) in view of Bandaru (US 20130079605). Claim 4 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Yamashita in view of Bandaru and Miller (US 10993657). Claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Yamashita in view of Bandaru and Rogers (US 20180064377). Claim 7 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Yamashita in view of Bandaru and Weitz (US 20170321177) and Prasad (US 20190069818). Claims 10 and 12 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Yamashita in view of Bandaru and Heikenfeld (US 20180353748).
Applicant traverses these rejections with respect to the now-pending claims.

Each of the rejections is premised on the Examiner's apparent contention that it would be obvious to adopt the skin patch shown in FIGS. 2(a) and 2(b) of Bandaru in the body fluid analyzer illustrated in FIG. 2 of Yamashita. The Examiner further apparently contends that Bandaru's skin patch corresponds to the mesh and vibration system of

independent claim 1. Without acquiescing to the Examiner's stated reasoning, Applicant has amended independent claim 1 herein to clarify the structure of the mesh nebulizer of the present disclosure, thereby clearly defining over the Examiner's proposed combination of references.
Attention is directed to FIGS. 2 and 3 of the present application, reproduced below for convenience.

FIG. 2
[portion of FIG. 3]

Referring to the figures above, independent claim 1 now clarifies that the mesh 12 has a first surface (lower surface in the figures) for location over a sweat surface on which sweat 32 is formed or collected, and that the mesh 12 includes openings extending through the mesh 12 from the first surface to an opposite second surface (upper surface in the figures) of the mesh 12. Independent claim 1 further clarifies that the vibration system 18 nebulizes the sweat 32 such that sweat 32 entering the openings in first surface of the mesh 12 is expelled as nebulized sweat droplets 33 from the second surface of the mesh 12. Additionally, independent claim 1 clarifies that the condensing unit 22 is located over the second surface of the mesh 12.
Attention is next directed to the cross-sectional views of FIGS. 2(a) and 2(b) of the skin patch of Bandaru shown below.
Fig 2(b)

As described in paragraph 0059 of Bandaru, the skin patch includes an ultrasonic transducer 1 placed at the top, followed by heating patterns 2. The heating patterns 2 includes resistive and/or inductive patterns functioning as heating elements. Below the heating patterns, electrodes 4 are printed on a flexible support material 3. Below those are a formulation compartment 6 and a medicated foam material 5. Reference number 7 denotes a reagent formulation/absorbent material used for the detection and the extraction/collection of analyte processes. Lastly, the patch includes a non-irritant adhesive 8 and release liner 9.

Quite clearly, the mesh nebulizer of amended claim 1 structurally defines over the skin patch of Bandaru. The skin patch of Bandaru does not include a mesh having openings extending therethrough, nor does it include a vibration system that nebulizes the sweat such that sweat entering the openings in a first surface of the mesh is expelled as nebulized sweat droplets from an opposite second surface of the mesh. Yamashita also fails to teach these features of independent claim 1.

Thus, even if the skin patch of Bandaru was somehow applied to the body fluid analyzer of Yamashita, the resultant combination would not render obvious the system recited in independent claim 1 and its dependent claims. Further, the additional secondary references applied against dependent claims 4, 5, 7 10 and 12 do not cure the deficiencies in the combined teachings of Yamashita and Bandaru.
It is therefore requested that the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be withdrawn.
Lastly, new claims 15-20 define over the teachings of the applied references for at least the same reasons as discussed above in connection with independent claim 1.

In view of the foregoing explanations, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider and reexamine the present application and pass the application to issue.
